R1-PROC.disposition: Recorded as historical procedural noncompliance. The original T001 iteration ran `uv self update 0.11.33` to bring a 0.11.24 workstation uv into the D025 range. R1 does not retroactively authorize that action; the disposition is preserved as honest history per the review's explicit decision (no clean-workstation rerun required because the repository candidate is not contaminated and the workstation is now inside the approved uv compatibility range). No further global/workstation tool mutation was performed during R1. Canonical verification for R1 used the currently installed compliant uv 0.11.33. See historical_procedural_findings[0] for the preserved record.

R1-REF.finding: `is_directory_or_extension_only()` previously returned True for every target beginning with `.`, exempting concrete dot-prefixed paths such as `./docs/ORCHESTRATOR-CHECKPOINTS.md` or `.github/workflows/check.yml` from mechanical resolution.
R1-REF.fix: Narrowed extension-only detection to a regex (`^\.[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9]+$`) that matches the form `.ext` (one dot followed by a bare identifier with no path separator). Concrete dot-prefixed paths containing a path separator or a bare filename component are now treated as concrete paths and remain eligible for mechanical resolution. The deliberate consumer-footprint exemptions for `.agent-coordination/` and `.agent-governance/` are preserved via `is_consumer_side_reference()` and were never coupled to the extension-only check.
regression_coverage_added: `test_extension_only_token_is_treated_as_prose` (parametrized over `.md`, `.py`, `.toml`, `.json`, `.lock`, `.yaml`, `.yml`): genuine extension tokens are exempted.

`test_concrete_dot_prefixed_path_is_not_exempted` (parametrized over `./docs/ORCHESTRATOR-CHECKPOINTS.md`, `.github/workflows/check.yml`, `./tests/test_reference_integrity.py`, `.python-version`, `./pyproject.toml`): concrete paths are not exempted.
`test_concrete_dot_prefixed_path_resolves_when_present`: a concrete dot-prefixed reference to an existing file resolves through the same machinery as any other concrete path.
`test_missing_concrete_dot_prefixed_path_is_classified_as_unresolved`: a missing concrete dot-prefixed path is classified as unresolved by the resolution helper, not silently ignored.

`test_reference_resolution_flags_concrete_dot_prefixed_paths`: the per-reference `_resolve()` helper reports `exists=False` for a missing concrete dot-prefixed path rather than classifying it as an exempt extension token.

R1-SCOPE.finding: The candidate added a 135-line generic Python `.gitignore` covering Django, Flask, Scrapy, Sphinx, Jupyter, mypy, pytype, Pyre, Cython, Rope, Spyder, pyenv, mkdocs, celery, sage, IPython, PyBuilder, packaging artifacts, and other ecosystems that T001 does not introduce.
R1-SCOPE.fix: Reduced `.gitignore` to a 30-line file justified by T001: Python bytecode/extension artifacts (`__pycache__/`, `*.py[cod]`, `*$py.class`, `*.so`), the uv-managed project environment (`.venv/`, `uv.lock.bak`), tool caches produced by the approved test/lint toolchain (`.pytest_cache/`, `.ruff_cache/`), the never-committed local secrets (`.env`), and ordinary OS/editor detritus (`.DS_Store`, `Thumbs.db`, `*.swp`, `*.swo`, `*~`, `.idea/`, `.vscode/`). A header comment records the policy: do not add framework/ecosystem boilerplate without a Task Contract revision that actually introduces that surface. The retained set is auditable: every entry corresponds to state actually produced by the T001 toolchain or to standard OS/editor detritus.

R2-REF-DOTFILE.fix: Replaced the broad bare-dotfile regex with an explicit allowlist of extension-only prose tokens used by canonical documentation. Other dot-prefixed tokens remain concrete path candidates.
regression_coverage_added: `.gitignore` is concrete and resolves when present.
`.missingconfig` is concrete and unresolved when absent.

R2-SCOPE-GITIGNORE.fix: Reduced `.gitignore` to `.venv/`, `__pycache__/`, `*.py[cod]`, `.pytest_cache/`, and `.ruff_cache/`; no additional T001-generated state is retained.

R2-REF-CONTAINMENT.fix: Canonicalized concrete targets with `Path.resolve(strict=False)` and compares canonical candidate/root paths before accepting containment.
R2-REF-CONTAINMENT.regression_coverage_added: `../outside.md` from a repository-root candidate is classified outside the repository without requiring an external file.

implementation_summary: R2 applies only the authorized reference-integrity and ignore-scope corrections on top of original T001 and R1. `tests/test_reference_integrity.py` uses explicit extension-only prose tokens, canonical candidate resolution, and focused dotfile/traversal regressions. `.gitignore` contains only five T001-authorized environment/cache patterns. No Markdown, dependencies, lockfile, external SDD/Skill assets, or global tools were changed.
implementation_rationale: Explicitly allowing only extension tokens used in canonical prose fails closed for dotfiles such as `.gitignore` and `.missingconfig`. Canonical `Path.resolve(strict=False)` makes parent traversal detectable even for missing paths. Consumer-footprint and directory exemptions remain separate. The retained ignore entries map directly to T001's local uv/Python/pytest/Ruff state.
